data.outcome_summary: The OECD PISA 2022 financial literacy factsheet for Italy reports students’ performance on a domain-specific assessment administered to 15-year-olds, with financial literacy measured for the fourth time (2012, 2015, 2018, 2022). Italy’s mean financial literacy score is 484, below the OECD average of 498, with 18% of students below Level 2 and 5% at Level 5. The factsheet also compares financial literacy to reading and mathematics, noting that about 73% of variation in financial literacy is explained by performance in mathematics and reading, while the remaining 27% reflects domain-specific factors. It further summarizes differences by gender and socioeconomic status, and reports associations between financial literacy levels and real-world financial behaviors (e.g., saving, comparing prices, online purchasing) and exposure to financial education at home and in school. Methodological details on sampling weights, PV combining, missing-data handling, and model specifications are not provided in the excerpt, limiting interpretability of any causal claims.
